title: Protocol for constructing an extensive cranial window utilizing a PEO-CYTOP nanosheet for in vivo wide-field imaging of the mouse brain
protocol: Anesthetize the adult mouse over 8 weeks old with isoflurane using an inhaled anesthetic.
Wipe the scalp hair with cotton swabs soaked in 70% ethanol.
Apply an eye ointment to protect against drying.
Remove the skin from the dorsal part of the head.
Apply local anesthesia to the skin, such as xylocaine.
Wait 3 minutes for the local anesthesia to take effect.
Cut the skin from the whole dorsal part of the head using scissors.
Push away the temporal and occipitalis muscle from the skull using tweezers.
Gently remove the periosteum on the skull surface using a scalpel or cotton swab.
Remove the periosteum entirely from the skull.
Place the head plate parallel to the transverse plane of the skull.
Apply dental resin (Super-Bond C&B Bulk-mix) to fix the head plate.
Ensure the entire exposed skull is covered with dental resin.
Wait 15 minutes for the dental resin to cure and solidify.
Administer GLYCEOL Injection via intraperitoneal injection at a dose of 15 μL per gram of body weight.
Drill the skull around the intentional craniotomy area using a drill bit (#140 ϕ1.4, Minitor, Japan).
Thin the drilled skull until bone thickness can be easily pushed down by low pressure with tweezers.
Move the drill bit in a circle along the edge of the craniotomy area to avoid injury to brain tissue.
Clear away bone debris from the groove using a cotton swab or air.
Soak the groove made by drilling with saline.
Insert tweezers between the skull and the brain surface gently remove the skull, leaving the dura intact.
Keep the tweezers parallel to avoid injuring the dura and brain tissue.
Slowly remove the skull while it is soaking in saline.
Stop bleeding using a sponge hemostat (Spongel) soaked in saline.
Cut PEO-CYTOP nanosheet and nonwoven fabric to a size suitable for covering the exposed brain area.
Glue the edges of the PEO-CYTOP nanosheet to seal the brain surface.
Add a few drops of saline to the brain surface.
Remove any excess water and slightly dry the surface using a paper towel or suction pump.
Place the PEO-CYTOP nanosheet on the brain with the hydrophilic side facing the brain surface.
Attach the PEO-CYTOP nanosheet to the brain surface by gently pushing it via the nonwoven fabric with tweezers.
Peel the nonwoven fabric away using tweezers.
Adjust the area of the PEO-CYTOP nanosheet covering the skull by scratching the area with tweezers.
Keep the edge of the nanosheet approximately 0.5 - 1 mm away from the exposed brain area.
Fix PEO-CYTOP nanosheet by gluing its edges to the head plate using ultraviolet curable resin.
Reduce intracranial pressure by administering GLYCEOL Injection via intraperitoneal injection if necessary.
Fix the mouse to the stage with a heating pad during the imaging session.
Anesthetize the mouse with 1.5% isoflurane during the imaging session.
